rationale.conceptual: The method is specific to the paper's discovery of the H-flip double-well potential and requires implementing a non-standard analysis (move H to backplane, relax, compute dynamic effective charge from dipole-moment slope). Several interacting components (geometry optimization, finite-difference charge extraction, volume measurement, correlation with bond angle) make it a genuine custom reproduction that demands careful implementation and physics understanding.
rationale.execution: The pipeline involves generating a 60-atom a-Si:H cell via melt-quench MD, then for each of at least six H sites performing normal and flipped relaxations, dipole-moment scans, volume calculations, and bond-angle measurements, followed by a NEB barrier calculation. This is a multi-stage workflow with around 4–6 major steps and tight coupling to an electronic-structure code (tight-binding or DFT), but the small system size keeps orchestration manageable.
